title: Lisandro Martinez to miss Manchester United’s trip to Everton due to injury
content:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez will miss his side’s game against Everton due to a suspected calf injury.

The 28-year-old had started United’s last nine Premier League matches and played the entirety of their last outing — the 1-1 draw with West Ham United on February 10.

Martinez, who has struggled with injuries throughout his United career, returned from a nine-month layoff in November after recovering from an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury to his left knee. United say they hope this latest problem will only keep him out for one to two weeks.

In the five games that Carrick has overseen, Martinez has been partnered with Harry Maguire at the heart of United’s defence. The pair have kept two clean sheets during that run, helping record wins over Manchester City (January 17), Arsenal (January 25), and Tottenham Hotspur (February 7).

Carrick praised the Argentina international following the victory at the Emirates Stadium in January, saying the emotion and excitement he wants his side to play with had been “epitomised” by Martinez in his performances in recent weeks.

Martinez’s injury could see one of Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven replace him in the starting XI. Matthijs de Ligt remains sidelined whilst recovering from a back problem that has ruled him out since November.

Carrick said last week that Mason Mount, who has missed United’s previous three fixtures with an injury sustained during training earlier this month, is “getting closer” to a return. The Athletic reported on January 27 that Patrick Dorgu is set to miss around 10 weeks with a hamstring injury.

United enter Monday’s game looking to cement their position in the top five and strengthen their Champions League hopes. They will be looking to capitalise on Chelsea’s 1-1 draw with Burnley on Saturday. A victory will see United leapfrog Chelsea into fourth place and three points behind third-place Aston Villa.

Additional reporting from Laurie Whitwell.
